paragraphs: Here's what I love about Asaph, friend. He sees an alliance of enemies plotting to erase God's people, and he doesn't panic, he doesn't scheme back, he PRAYS. He opens with "O God, be not silent," and he says it three different ways (Psalm 83:1). When the whole world feels lined up against you, the first move is to take it to God, out loud and honest.

Now watch the turn, because this is the heart of it. Asaph asks God to cover their faces with shame, and he says what it's for: "that they may seek Your name, O LORD" (Psalm 83:16). He ends by asking that they may know "that You alone, whose name is the LORD, are Most High over all the earth" (Psalm 83:18). I think that tells us what Asaph wanted most. Not just for his enemies to lose, but for God to be known as God.

So what does that mean for you, baker? Some days it will feel like the odds are stacked up against you, like an alliance of ten against one. This psalm says you can bring all of it to God, the big plots and the big fears, and you can trust that He is Most High over all the earth. That's one steady truth to stand on. And I'll tell you, it beats standing on a wobbly cookie rack.
